Cc: ops@greenstripe.com

Subject: Severe latency + 500s after today's model update

Hi Sean,

We started seeing a spike in tail latency and 5xx errors starting ~08:40 UTC after you pushed the model update this morning (v3.0 with the new q4_lowmem quant profile). Our production payments flow is timing out on several critical endpoints — error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 4.7% and median latency increased ~210ms per request. Attached are a condensed set of request IDs and the client-side traces (inference-logs-20260501.zip).

Two urgent asks:
- Can you rollback the change for our org to the previous model ASAP?
- We need temporary mitigation (routing to older variant or increased timeouts) while you investigate.

This is impacting checkout flows; leadership is already on calls. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Alex Li
Head of Platform Engineering
GreenStripe

Team — quick technical readout from the initial triage:

What we see:
- The v3.0 model build with quantization profile `q4_lowmem` introduced a new kernel selection path. For certain sequence-length distributions (GreenStripe uses batched long-context payment receipts) the runtime is falling back to a slower KV cache path. That fallback ends up streaming partial state to CPU memory which increases per-token latency ~180–250ms and in tight memory pressure cases triggers transient OOMs producing server 500s.
- Error traces attached (stacktrace-v3.0-q4_lowmem.txt) show mismatched allocation sizes on the cuKV layer and repeated memcpy fallbacks.

Immediate remediation options (priority order):
A) Fast rollback: route GreenStripe traffic back to v2.6 stable variant (no quant) — lowest risk and fastest (can be done within 30–45 minutes).
B) Patch: push a hotfix to kernel selector to avoid the `q4_lowmem` path for long-context batches — estimated 4–6 hours including validation.
C) Temporary throttle: enforce stricter batching limits for GreenStripe to avoid long sequences (buying time but may reduce throughput).

Recommendation: do Plan A immediately and then follow with Plan B for a permanent fix. I’ll attach the full trace and a short runbook.

—Rohan Mehta
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — rolling back to v2.6 and the canary approach is fine with us. Appreciate the quick turnaround and the offered credit. Two requests before you close the ticket:

1) Can you add a QA gating step for any quantized model variant that includes a long-context customer profile in the canary matrix?
2) Please add a per-account regression monitor that alerts on >1% absolute error-rate increase or >150ms median latency uplift post-rollout.

Once those are in your remediation plan, we’ll mark this as resolved on our side. Looking forward to the postmortem.

Best,
Alex Li
